comparator.name: Marine Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official handbook defines 180 EC: 135 EC of named compulsory study, a 3-EC restricted mathematics/statistics choice, a 12-EC bachelor thesis and 30 EC of open electives. Mathematics Applied: Introduction is selected by the official-order tie-break.
components: Boundary Crossing and Personal Leadership in Marine Sciences
Global Water Systems and Climate Change
Research Methodology for Human Environment Interactions
Introduction to Law for the Life and Social Sciences
Global Marine Compounds, Flows, and Cycles
Life History and Biology of Aquatic Animals
Evaluation and Design of Marine Nature-Based Solutions
Assessment of Marine Nature Based Solutions
Selected by official-order tie-break from the 3-EC mathematics/statistics restricted choice.
Genuine open elective space; no minor or course package is invented.

alternatives.label: Marine socio-ecological systems & sustainability
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines marine biology, ecology, water and Earth systems with economics, governance, justice, data and applied sustainability research.
alternatives.concept: A closest feasible marine-sciences response integrating ocean ecology and biology with climate, water, economics, governance, social dependence and research on sustainable socio-ecological systems.
progression: Sustainability, ecology, economics, research and biological foundations precede water systems, spatial evidence, marine biology, environmental biogeochemistry, governance and applied sustainability research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Marine ecology, biodiversity & conservation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres ecology, evolution, biodiversity, conservation, physiology, marine biology, environmental chemistry and quantitative field research.
alternatives.concept: Develops the evidenced ocean-life and conservation direction through ecology, evolution, biodiversity, physiology, marine biology, environmental chemistry and conservation research.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes marine ecology, evolution, biodiversity and conservation the organising priority. It differs from the integrated socio-ecological programme by nine courses and 67.5 EC.
progression: Biology, ecology, sustainability and quantitative foundations precede evolution, ecosystems, conservation, marine biology, environmental biogeochemistry and applied research. Formal prerequisites and offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Ocean climate, coasts & spatial evidence
alternatives.concept: Develops the evidenced ocean-climate, coastal-system and offshore-energy direction through climate science, water, hazards, Earth observation, spatial evidence and renewable-system design.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres climate, water, hazards, Earth observation, environmental systems, spatial data, renewable systems and applied resilience research.
progression: Earth-system, climate, water, ecology, economics and data foundations precede hazards, Earth observation, environmental systems, renewable design and applied resilience research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes ocean climate, coastal systems, offshore energy and spatial evidence the organising priority. It differs from the closest programme by ten courses and from the marine-ecology direction by twelve courses.

core: Marine socio-ecological systems, ocean life and biodiversity
Marine ecology, aquaculture, food systems and conservation
Ocean, coastal and climate processes, energy and nature-based solutions
Marine economics, governance, law, policy and dependent communities
Fieldwork, geo-information, modelling, data analysis and independent marine research
adjacent: Ocean climate, coastal systems and offshore energy
questions: How can marine ecosystems be conserved while oceans support food, energy and livelihoods?
How can climate, coastal and spatial evidence guide sustainable ocean decisions?
How can biological and social research support marine conservation and nature-based solutions?

selection.assessment: The closest programme integrates marine ecology, water, economics, governance and society. Marine ecology/conservation and ocean-climate/coastal systems support two further coherent, feasible and pairwise-distinct directions. Production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: WUR offers a dedicated marine-sciences curriculum with marine fieldwork, ocean biophysical processes, marine food systems, aquaculture, marine economics, governance, nature-based solutions, modelling and a marine thesis. UCR can combine substantial ecology, marine biology, climate, water, spatial evidence, economics and governance, but does not reproduce that specialist marine sequence course for course.
